t: List Of Chinese Troops Controlled By General Chiang

pages.en:
(C.I.D.) Office Notes

A/D.C.I.

Attached is an up-to-date list in tabular form
of Chinese troops controlled by General Chiang Kai-shek,
Marshal Feng Yu-hsiang, Marshal Yen Shih-san and General
Chang Hsueh-liang.

I respectfully beg to suggest that copies be
sent to the Authorities concerned.

E. Park
D. S. I.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE C.I.D. RECORDS File No. C. D. 611 November. 9, 1929.）

（批：Mc）

（批：For O'Leau, British, American
Consuls & Mukden）

（批：See）

（批：Instructions carried out
on November 9.
MC
11/9/29）
pages.zh:
（刑事调查处）办公室备忘录

助理刑事调查处长

随函附上蒋介石将军、冯玉祥元帅、阎锡山元帅及张学良将军所辖中国部队的最新列表，以表格形式呈现。

卑职谨建议将副本送交有关当局。

E. Park
副刑事调查处长

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处刑事调查处档案 档案号 C. D. 611 1929年11月9日。）

（批：Mc）

（批：致欧利瑞（O'Leau）、英国领事、美国领事及沈阳）

（批：阅）

（批：指令已于11月9日执行。
MC
1929年11月9日）

In the above four provinces (Manchuria and Jehol), there are 39 mixed brigades of 10,000 men in each brigade, bringing the total to 390,000. Among these are included : 25,000 artillerists, 60,000 cavalrymen, and 10,000 members of the Labour Corps. At the commencement of the Sino-Soviet dispute, Marshal Chang organized half of the above troops into two army corps which are now serving at the front. The commander of the 1st Corps is General Chang Tso-hsiang and that of the 2nd Corps, General Yu Tseng. Besides, there are in his commission 12 armoured trains and his fleet consists of some 50 cruisers, gunboats, etc. The latter is under the command of Admiral Sung Hung-lieh. His air forces consist of

In Szechuen :

General Yang Seng (楊森) has about 40,000 troops stationeu in the eastern part.

General Liu Hsiang (劉湘) has about 60,000 troops stationeu in the southern part.

General Liu Wen-hwei (劉文輝) has about 50,000 troops stationed in the western part.

General Liu Cheng-hou (劉存厚) has about 10,000 troops stationed in the northern part.

General Lan Sing-hwei (賴心輝) has some 30,000 troops stationed also in the southern part (Kaohsien and Yunning)

General Tien Chung-yao (田頌堯) has some 30,000 troops stationed also in the norther part.

General Teng Sih-hou (鄧錫侯) has about 40,000 troops stationed in Chengtu and vicinity.

All these generals only look after their own interests within the area they occupy, and are constantly at variance with each other over conflict of interests. They have little relation with the National Government at Nanking.

邓锡侯将军约有 40,000 名 troops 驻扎在成都及周边地区。

这些将军只关心其在占领区内的自身利益，并因利益冲突而
不断相互争执。他们与南京国民政府关系甚微。
